images.alt: A Xerox Star 8010 workstation with its cabinet, black-and-white bitmapped display, keyboard and mouse, photographed at a vintage computer show
images.caption: A Xerox Star 8010, announced 27 April 1981 as the Information System — a bitmapped screen, a mouse, and icons for documents and folders, sold as a finished product with a price list and a service contract.

images.alt: A collection of vintage computers including a Xerox Star workstation with its distinctive keyboard and display
images.caption: The Star's cabinet stood on the floor beside the desk, the size of a two-drawer filing cabinet, driving the 1024x808 display on top of it.

images.alt: A Xerox Star computer on display at a vintage computer exhibition
images.caption: A Star preserved and running at a vintage computer fair — one of only a low tens of thousands ever sold.

images.alt: A close-up view of the icon-based desktop interface on a Xerox Star 8010 monitor
images.caption: Icons for documents, folders and printers on the Star's ViewPoint desktop — the vocabulary every graphical interface since has borrowed from.
